Restore your smile

A permanent
tooth replacement.

A missing tooth is about more than appearance. It can shift neighboring teeth, weaken the jawbone over time, and make everyday chewing and speaking more difficult. At Shades Creek Dental in Homewood, AL, dental implants solve all of this at the root. An implant is a small titanium post that acts as a replacement tooth root, anchoring a custom crown, bridge, or denture securely in place. The result is a stable, natural-looking tooth that blends seamlessly with the rest of your smile and can last for decades.

Dr. Ron MacBeth plans every implant with precision using 3D cone beam imaging, so your new tooth fits your bite perfectly and looks completely natural. Whether you are replacing a single tooth, several teeth, or an entire arch, our goal is a result you can be proud of and trust for years to come. Because we place and restore implants right here in our Homewood office, you receive consistent, coordinated care from a team that already knows you and your smile.

What a dental implant is

Three parts.
One tooth.

Part 01 — The post

The root.

A small, biocompatible titanium screw placed into the jawbone to act as an artificial tooth root. Over time it fuses with the surrounding bone through a natural process called osseointegration, creating a foundation as stable as a natural root.

Fuses with the bone over the following months.

Part 02 — The abutment

The connector.

A connector that attaches to the top of the post, joining the implant below the gum to the restoration above it. It is fitted once the post has fused with the jawbone, and it is what allows your final crown, bridge, or denture to sit securely in your bite.

Attached once the implant has healed.

Part 03 — The restoration

The tooth.

The visible part — a custom crown, bridge, or denture, crafted to match your natural teeth. Because the implant replaces the root as well as the crown, it provides unmatched stability, protects the jawbone, and functions just like a natural tooth.

Shaded and shaped to match your surrounding teeth.

The doctor's approach

What would I do if this was my tooth?

The questions Dr. MacBeth works through before recommending treatment — not a self-assessment.

  1. 01

    Can the tooth be saved?

  2. 02

    What does the root need?

  3. 03

    What will provide the best long-term foundation?

  4. 04

    What is the plan?

01 — Can the tooth be saved?

That is always the first question. If a tooth cannot be kept, the decision moves to what replaces it — because when a tooth is lost and not replaced, the effects extend far beyond the empty space.

02 — What does the root need?

The bone beneath a missing tooth begins to shrink, because it no longer receives stimulation from a tooth root. An implant replaces that root — a titanium post placed into the jawbone, restoring what was lost below the gum, not only what shows above it.

03 — What will provide the best long-term foundation?

  • FunctionAnchored securely, so you can eat the foods you love without worry or slipping.
  • StabilityThe post fuses with the jawbone through osseointegration, creating a foundation as stable as a natural root.
  • AestheticsThe restoration is shaded and shaped to match your surrounding teeth.

04 — What is the plan?

The right treatment starts with the right diagnosis.

Dr. MacBeth plans every implant with 3D cone beam imaging, so your new tooth fits your bite perfectly and looks completely natural.

Why replacing it matters

What happens if you leave the gap.

When a tooth is lost and not replaced, the effects extend far beyond the empty space.

  • 01

    Neighbouring teeth drift

    The teeth beside the gap can gradually tilt or drift into it, throwing off your bite and making teeth harder to clean.

  • 02

    The opposing tooth over-erupts

    The tooth opposite the gap may begin to over-erupt, and the added strain can lead to uneven wear and jaw discomfort.

  • 03

    The jawbone shrinks

    The bone beneath a missing tooth begins to shrink over time because it no longer receives stimulation from a tooth root. This can change your facial appearance and make future treatment more complex.

Replacing a missing tooth promptly with a dental implant helps protect your remaining teeth, preserve your jawbone, and maintain your overall oral health.

The advantages

Why implants became the preferred choice.

  • A natural look and feel

    Your custom restoration is shaded and shaped to match your surrounding teeth, so no one will know it is not your own.

  • Long-lasting durability

    With proper care, dental implants can last for decades, making them a dependable long-term investment in your smile.

  • Protection for your jawbone

    Implants stimulate the jaw like a natural tooth root, helping prevent the bone loss that follows missing teeth.

  • A stable, comfortable bite

    Because implants are anchored securely, you can eat the foods you love without worry or slipping.

  • No damage to healthy teeth

    Unlike a traditional bridge, an implant does not rely on grinding down the teeth beside it.

  • Preserved facial structure

    Replacing missing teeth and bone helps maintain the natural shape and fullness of your face.

  • Easy maintenance

    You care for an implant just like a natural tooth, with regular brushing, flossing, and checkups.

  • Improved confidence

    A complete, secure smile lets you speak, laugh, and eat without hesitation.

Solutions for every need

Four ways to
rebuild a smile.

01

Single tooth implant

A single implant topped with a custom crown replaces one missing tooth without affecting the neighboring teeth.

02

Implant-supported bridge

When several teeth in a row are missing, a bridge anchored by implants replaces them without relying on natural teeth for support.

03

Implant-supported dentures

For patients missing most or all of their teeth, implants can secure a denture firmly in place, eliminating the slipping associated with traditional dentures.

04

Full mouth dental implants

A complete solution that restores an entire arch of teeth using a set of strategically placed implants for maximum stability.

During your consultation, we will help you determine which option best fits your smile, your goals, and your long-term oral health.

Candidacy

Are you a candidate?

You may be an ideal candidate if

  • You are missing one or more teeth
  • You are in generally good health
  • You have healthy gums
  • You have enough jawbone to support the implant
  • You are tired of ill-fitting dentures
  • You want a permanent alternative to a bridge

Things we would discuss first

  • Bone loss — grafting can often rebuild the foundation
  • Uncontrolled health conditions
  • Gum disease
  • Smoking

Many of these can be managed or addressed before treatment.

The best way to find out if implants are right for you is a personalized consultation. Dr. MacBeth will evaluate your oral health, take 3D imaging, and help you understand your options so you can make a confident, informed decision.

Step by step

The dental implant process.

Getting a dental implant is a carefully planned process designed to ensure a strong, lasting result. While every treatment plan is personalized, here is what the journey typically looks like at our Homewood office.

  1. Consultation and planning

    Dr. MacBeth examines your mouth, takes 3D cone beam imaging, and creates a detailed treatment plan tailored to you.

  2. Preparatory treatment if needed

    In some cases, procedures like bone grafting or extractions are completed first to prepare a healthy foundation.

  3. Implant placement

    The titanium implant post is precisely placed into the jawbone during a comfortable, minimally invasive procedure.

  4. Healing and osseointegration

    Over the following months, the implant fuses with the bone to create a stable anchor.

  5. Abutment placement

    Once healed, the abutment is attached to connect the implant to your final restoration.

  6. Placing your restoration

    Your custom crown, bridge, or denture is secured, completing your new smile.

  7. Follow-up care

    We check your implant and restoration to ensure everything looks, fits, and functions beautifully.

One of the great advantages of dental implants is how easy they are to maintain. You care for an implant just as you would a natural tooth. Brush twice a day, floss daily to keep the area around the implant clean and healthy, and keep up with your regular dental checkups and cleanings. These visits allow us to monitor your implant and the surrounding gums to ensure everything stays in great shape.

Avoiding habits like chewing ice or using your teeth as tools helps protect your restoration, and if you grind your teeth, a nightguard can add extra protection. With good care, your dental implant can last for decades, making it one of the most reliable investments you can make in your smile.

Frequently asked questions

About dental implants.

01What is a dental implant?

A dental implant is a small titanium post that replaces the root of a missing tooth. It is placed into the jawbone, where it fuses with the bone to create a stable foundation. A custom crown, bridge, or denture is then attached, giving you a replacement tooth that looks, feels, and functions like a natural one.

02How long do dental implants last?

With proper care, dental implants can last for decades and often a lifetime. The implant post itself is designed to be permanent, while the restoration on top may eventually need replacement due to normal wear. Good oral hygiene and regular checkups are key to maximizing the lifespan of your implant.

03Does getting a dental implant hurt?

Most patients are surprised by how comfortable the procedure is. The area is fully numbed during placement, so you should not feel pain during the surgery. Some mild soreness or swelling afterward is normal and typically resolves within a few days, and it is easily managed for the vast majority of patients.

04How much do dental implants cost?

The cost depends on factors such as how many implants you need, whether any preparatory treatment like bone grafting is required, and the type of restoration. Because every case is unique, we provide a personalized estimate during your consultation and review your options and any out-of-pocket costs with you.

05How long does the dental implant process take?

The full process often spans several months, mainly because the implant needs time to fuse with the jawbone. The placement procedure itself is relatively quick, but the healing period ensures a strong, lasting result. Dr. MacBeth will give you a personalized timeline based on your specific treatment plan.

06Am I a good candidate for dental implants?

Most adults with one or more missing teeth and generally good oral and overall health are good candidates. Adequate jawbone and healthy gums help support the implant, though bone grafting can rebuild the foundation if needed. A consultation with 3D imaging is the best way to confirm whether implants are right for you.

07What is osseointegration?

Osseointegration is the natural process by which the titanium implant post fuses with the surrounding jawbone. This fusion is what gives dental implants their exceptional stability, allowing them to function like a natural tooth root. It typically takes a few months and is essential to the long-term success of the implant.

08Can dental implants replace multiple missing teeth?

Yes. Implants are versatile enough to replace a single tooth, several teeth, or a full arch. Options include single tooth implants, implant-supported bridges, and implant-supported dentures. Dr. MacBeth will recommend the solution that best fits the number and location of your missing teeth.

09What is bone grafting and might I need it?

Bone grafting rebuilds jawbone that has been lost due to missing teeth, gum disease, or other factors. It creates a strong enough foundation to support an implant. Not everyone needs it, but if imaging shows insufficient bone, a graft can make implants possible. We will let you know if it is part of your plan.

10How do I care for my dental implants?

Care for your implant just as you would a natural tooth. Brush twice a day, floss daily, and keep up with regular dental checkups and cleanings. Avoid chewing hard objects like ice, and if you grind your teeth, ask us about a nightguard. Good daily care helps your implant last for many years.

11Are dental implants better than dentures or bridges?

Implants offer advantages that dentures and bridges cannot match. They stand on their own without relying on or damaging neighboring teeth, they prevent the jawbone loss that comes with missing teeth, and they provide a stable, permanent, natural feel. Dr. MacBeth can help you compare all your options and choose what suits you best.

12Does insurance cover dental implants?

Coverage varies by plan. Some dental insurance plans cover part of the implant process, such as the restoration, while others offer limited or no implant coverage. Our team will help you understand your benefits and any out-of-pocket costs before treatment begins. Call 205-417-2750 with questions about your specific plan.
